analysis.rootCauseHypothesis:
The hosting side is likely failing to persist or locate the project data needed to build the backup, so the export handler thinks no valid saved backup exists. A second possibility is that the backup generator is broken due to a misconfigured storage path or permissions issue on the server, causing the file never to be created even after save. Underlying error: TEST FAILURE

The project backup download did not work — the app reports no backup was created and no downloadable .pixibun file was produced.

Observations:
- Clicking 'Download project backup' repeatedly resulted in the dialog message: 'No backup was created. Your project is still open here.'
- A 'Save' was executed and a subsequent 'Download project backup' attempt still produced the same message and no file download.
- The UI shows the project name 'Challenge portable backup' and two frames (preconditions met), so the backup generator appears to be broken in this build/instance.

recommendedFixTarget.rationale: Inspect the server-side backup export route and the persistence layer it depends on. The most likely issue is that the app is only creating a backup when it can read a saved project record from the host, but the current instance never persists the project state (or persists it under the wrong user/session/project id), so the download endpoint returns 'no backup created.' Verify that 'Save' actually writes to the backing store, that the backup job is triggered after save, and that the generated backup file is placed in the expected download location with the correct .pixibun content type/filename. Also check for environment-specific problems on the host such as disabled filesystem write permissions, misconfigured temp/output directory, or a broken route/worker that generates the archive. Fix by restoring write access or correcting the backup generation pipeline so the project state is serialized and streamed as a downloadable .pixibun file.
